items.title: Grok Bot Linux: Install Grok Bot on Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora
items.content:
Grok Bot Linux support is official: the desktop app runs on Linux x64 and Arm64 as a.deb, an.rpm or an AppImage. And here’s a detail most people miss: the cloud computer your Bots actually work on runs Linux too. Below is how to install it on Ubuntu, Debian or Fedora, how updates work through apt and dnf, how to hold a version, and the few things that behave differently on Linux, all from xAI’s official docs. My video is right under this intro.

Key takeaways

- Runs on Linux x64 and Arm64:.deb,.rpm or AppImage.

- The.deb and.rpm add a signed package repository.

- Update with `apt` or `dnf`; AppImage updates itself.

- Security keys and some notification routing aren’t on Linux yet.

## Which Linux formats Grok Bot supports

The Grok Bot FAQ lists Linux on x64 and Arm64, as a.deb package, an.rpm package or an AppImage. Download it from x.ai/bot, the download page or the Grok Bot page of your Cursor dashboard.

## Install on Ubuntu or Debian

Install the.deb with your usual tool. The deployment guide says it adds a signed apt repository at `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/grok-bot.sources`, so new versions arrive with your normal upgrades. To update by hand:

```
sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade grok-bot
```

## How to install Grok Bot on Windows

The Get Started guide says the desktop app runs on Windows (x64 and Arm64) and checks for updates on its own. Get the installer from any of these:

- x.ai/bot

- The Download Grok Bot row on the Grok Bot dashboard page

- The download page, which lists the current installer for every platform

Run the Setup.exe, choose Sign in and finish sign-in in your browser. Grok Bot uses your Cursor account; there’s no separate login. Your first Bot, named Grok Bot, is set up after a short intro.

The installer works per user: it installs into your profile under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, so you don’t need admin rights for a normal install.

## Your PC vs the Bot’s cloud computer

This is the part most people get wrong. Per the deployment guide, Bots do their work on a hosted computer in the cloud, one per member, running Linux. The Windows app is a client for chat, review and approvals.

That’s why closing your laptop doesn’t stop a routine, and why files that exist only on your Windows machine aren’t covered by the Bot computer’s backups. The computer and apps guide says to keep your own backups for those.

## Check this setting first: local access

A Bot can only run commands on your own PC when that’s enabled and you approve it. In Settings → Computer → Your computer, set Execution on this computer to:

- Ask every time (the default): approve each command.

- Always allow: no prompts.

- Never allow: Bots can’t touch your PC.

## Sign-ins, Windows Hello and security keys

The Bot’s browser runs on the cloud computer, so some sign-in methods don’t carry over. The troubleshooting guide says Windows Hello, fingerprint, Face ID and passkeys saved on your laptop don’t work on the Bot’s computer. Instead, choose Take over, sign in with a method your company allows there, then I’m done.

Windows does get one extra: hardware security keys such as a YubiKey. For passwords, use Vault or a Secure Form, never ordinary chat.

The Windows app updates itself. In Settings → Updates you’ll find Check for Updates and Restart to Update. Automatic Updates is on by default: a downloaded update installs while you’re away (screen locked or idle for 10+ minutes and Grok Bot not busy).

Don’t fall behind. The troubleshooting guide says Grok Bot requires an update when your version is more than 14 days old and a newer one is out, and covers the window with Update required. Your Bots keep running in the cloud while you update. Updating the app doesn’t reset the cloud computer; that’s a separate Update Bot’s Computer button.

The deployment guide covers fleets. On Windows, push the Setup.exe with Intune, Configuration Manager or another distribution tool and install silently:

```
Grok_Bot_{version}_Setup.exe /S
```

Grok Bot iOS support is official: the Grok Bot app runs on iPhone with iOS 18 or later and on iPad with iPadOS 18 or later, from the App Store. My video is right under this intro.

- Sign in with the same Cursor account as desktop.

- Bots can use Calendar, Contacts, Location, Alarms, Reminders and Home.

## What Grok Bot on iOS does

The Grok Bot for Mobile page describes the iPhone app as the way to start work, answer questions, approve steps and review results away from your desk. It connects to the same Bots, conversations, routines, connectors and shared cloud computer as the desktop app.

Your iPhone doesn’t do the heavy work. Bots run on a hosted computer in the cloud, so closing the app, or your phone going to sleep, doesn’t stop a background turn or routine. The FAQ confirms it: closing the app, laptop or phone doesn’t stop the work.

New to it? Read what Grok Bot is first.

## How to install Grok Bot on iPhone and iPad

- You need an iPhone on iOS 18 or later, or an iPad on iPadOS 18 or later.

- An eligible Grok Bot plan (see the X Subscription page).

- Download Grok Bot from the App Store.

Open the app, choose Log In or Sign Up, and finish Cursor sign-in in the browser with the same Cursor account you use on desktop. If your access comes from a SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription, choose Link Grok Account, then Finished Linking? Refresh My Status. A link you made on desktop works on the phone too.

If your plan already includes Grok Bot, the docs say not to buy a second subscription through Apple. Allow notifications on first run if you want alerts; the docs note iPhone push delivery is rolling out gradually.

## Siri, Shortcuts, Live Activities and the Action Button

This is where the iPhone app pulls ahead. Grok Bot adds four shortcuts you can run from Siri, Spotlight or the Shortcuts app:

- List Bots

- Send Message: for example, say “Send a message in Grok Bot.”

- Start Dictation: dictate to a Bot without opening the app while your iPhone is unlocked. A Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island shows progress, with cancel and send buttons.

- Start Voice Chat: talk to a Bot live, also shown as a Live Activity.

On an iPhone with an Action Button, go to Settings → Action Button, swipe to Shortcut, and choose Grok Bot > Start Voice Chat. One press and you’re talking to your Bot; press again to hang up.

## Messaging and the share sheet

In a conversation you can type, dictate, start a voice chat, play a voice memo, attach photos and files, mention Bots or `@everyone`, reply in threads and react. When a Bot drafts an email or Slack message, you can edit it, then choose Send or Discard.

On iPhone the system share sheet works fully: share a photo, file, link or text, choose Grok Bot, pick a chat and tap Attach. The item lands in that chat’s composer. (On Android the share sheet takes text only for now.)

## Let a Bot use your iPhone’s apps

In your own chat with a Bot you own, a Bot can use these apps when you ask:

- Calendar: read, add, change or delete events (not repeating ones; it never invites anyone).

- Contacts: read-only lookups by name.

- Location: your current position.

- Alarms: an alarm or a timer of up to 24 hours. These need a newer iOS than the app itself; if your iPhone can’t, Alarms won’t appear.

- Reminders (iPhone only): read, add, change, check off or delete.

- Home (iPhone only): lights, fans, blinds, thermostats, locks, garage doors and security systems.

Grant access in Settings → Connect apps → iPhone (or iPad). Grok Bot must be open on the phone for the Bot to reach it. Locks, garage doors and security systems follow the same approval rules as other Home changes, so keep Auto Review on.

## Approvals, the computer and routines

Open the computer from a chat to watch work, inspect the screen, or take over for a password, a two-factor code or a CAPTCHA, then tap I’m done. If your team admin set a device limit, it shows under Manage your devices as Ask every time, Never allow or Always allow.

Routines live on each Bot’s profile: see the schedule, next run and run history, toggle Active, swipe to delete, or use Edit routine and Add routine. My Grok Bot templates guide has ready-made ideas.

## Billing and what stays on desktop

Apple handles any subscription you buy in the app, including App Store free trials. Cancel or change it in Apple ID → Subscriptions before a trial ends if you don’t want it to convert. Cursor can’t cancel or refund an in-app plan for you. Only monthly individual plans are sold in the app.
